comments.text: That girl was right, the stylist is still a person.  She got that part right.  But what does that really mean.  She trying to play it off that telling these things on the internet has in some way victimized the stylist.  Umm. No, honey.  You just pointed out how far out of bounds the stylist AND the salon really were.  They are people and as people they should have approached that customer with every ounce of respect they were clearly demanding of her in return.  They should have acted like a person and seen the mistake, admitted the mistake and corrected the situation.  If the stylist or the salon owner want to be seen as a person, themselves, then they should have treated that customer like a person and fixed it to the best of their ability or refunded her so that she could have someone else help her correct the damage. I have had similar situations twice in my life and both times it was acknowledged, apologized for and corrected immediately.  The situations were at two different places and both reacted in an understanding manner.  That is the difference between people who take pride in their work and care about the people they work for, the customers.  It should never be let go when a business mistreats the customers.  It is best to let others know and warn them before they end up in the same situation.  Reputable businesses don't have an issue with helping to rectify situations like this and the customers don't have to take days running someone down to even talk to them about the problem.  You are not harming other stylists or businesses by speaking out about shady places like that.

I just heard her say that the stylist warned her that her hair could melt. That ends this whole conversation.

What more could a stylist do? 
Deny the client the service. I bet many hair stylists will be telling people no now from this incident. I’m not a hair stylist but if I was I wouldn’t dare risk doing this girls hair knowing it could melt even if she said do it anyway. People are desperate to have what they want done regardless of the professional advice they are given and the warnings, then when someone says ok to appease the person…all of a sudden it’s the person who took a chance to deliver what the person wanted’s fault. I feel sorry for the stylist. 

The stylist told her the risk in advance.
Let this be a cautionary tale to all hair stylists: protect yourselves from clients that want unrealistic work done on their hair and send them away unhappy because you wouldn’t do it for them—instead of them being unhappy when you do what they want anyway and then end up with your name slandered on the internet.
